Business API map: Bunkai TMS

Generated 2026-11-13 from the staging OpenAPI spec (111 endpoints) and upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging 63d5e7e3. Narrative only: the endpoint catalog is the OpenAPI spec.

Executive summary

Bunkai's API lets three kinds of callers run a test-management workspace end to end. People work in the browser with a Supabase session cookie. Machines (CLI tools, AI agents, CI pipelines) use a Bearer personal access token (bk_pat_*) against the same /api/v1 routes. Systems call in too: Stripe posts signed webhooks and Vercel Cron triggers two daily jobs with a shared secret.

The business loop the API closes: a team imports User Stories from its own Jira, authors ATCs anchored to those stories, assembles them into Tests, executes Runs (by hand, streamed step by step, or submitted already finished by an agent), files Bugs from failed steps, and reads coverage and traceability back. Workspaces pay for their plan through Stripe Checkout. The plan is applied only when Stripe confirms the payment.

Every route goes through one gateway, withApiHandler(), that is secure by default: a route is authenticated unless it opts into public, and most routes also name the capabilities the caller must hold. Data isolation between workspaces lives in Postgres Row Level Security, also for PAT callers, whose queries run under a short-lived per-user JWT. Multi-table writes go through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, so a write either fully lands or fully rolls back.

Permission and auth model

Route postures

Each route declares one posture in withApiHandler(handler, options). The posture is the first gate; RLS is the last.

PostureWho gets throughTypical routesWhere enforced
public (11 routes)Anyone. Some carry their own secret instead.health, API index, auth/{check-email,signup,signin,confirm,resend,magic-link}, billing/webhook (Stripe signature), admin/send-digest and admin/storage-cleanup (CRON_SECRET)lib/api/handler.ts; the route's own signature or secret check
cookie-only (14 files)A browser session. A Bearer PAT is refused with 403.tokens (a PAT never mints or revokes a PAT), me/active-workspace, workspace delete/restore, membership, data exportlib/api/handler.ts
authenticated (14 files)Any signed-in principal, no capability needed. Each use carries a written reason.identity and other no-capability readslib/api/handler.ts
required (84 files)A principal holding every listed capability.the bulk of the product API: ATCs, tests, runs, bugs, imports, billinglib/api/handler.ts + lib/api/capabilities.ts

Capabilities

One vocabulary of four capabilities lives in lib/api/capabilities.ts: atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin. A cookie session implicitly holds all four, so for browser users the real limit is their workspace role plus RLS. A PAT holds only the scopes it was minted with. Headless sign-in mints DEFAULT_PAT_SCOPES, which never include workspace:admin. An admin-scoped token comes only from POST /api/v1/tokens, and only for an owner or admin of the target workspace (BK-134/135).

Schemes

  • Session cookie: password sign-in (POST /api/v1/auth/signin), sign-up with a mandatory six-digit OTP (signup then confirm), magic link, or OAuth with GitHub or Google (GET /auth/oauth/{provider}, PKCE plus a state check in /auth/callback).
  • Bearer PAT: returned by signin and confirm, or minted from a session at POST /api/v1/tokens. The secret is shown once. Verification: prefix lookup, hash compare, expiry and revocation check. An admin-scoped PAT is re-bound to its issuing workspace on every call, not only at mint time.
  • Signed system calls: Stripe signs the raw webhook body; Vercel Cron sends CRON_SECRET as a Bearer value. Neither carries a user identity.
  • Magic link rail (BK-400): /auth/callback now verifies a token_hash statelessly, which lets a link requested on one device open on another. The legacy PKCE code path stays for links already in flight.
  1. The machine caller posts email and password to POST /api/v1/auth/signin.
  2. Supabase Auth verifies the password and returns a session.
  3. The API mints a PAT with the default scopes and returns it with the session.
  4. Later calls carry Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_...; the gateway finds the token by prefix and compares the hash.
  5. The gateway checks the route's required capabilities against the token's scopes.
  6. The handler queries Postgres as the token's user, so RLS applies exactly as for that person in the browser.
  7. The answer uses the standard error/success envelope.

Journey: new user onboarding (browser)

A first-time visitor creates an account and their first workspace, the minimum to start working in Bunkai.

  1. POST /api/v1/auth/check-email tells the page whether to show sign-in or sign-up.
  2. POST /api/v1/auth/signup creates the user; Supabase emails a six-digit code. There is no confirmation bypass.
  3. POST /api/v1/auth/confirm verifies the code, opens the session and returns a default-scope PAT. POST /api/v1/auth/resend re-sends the code.
  4. The onboarding form calls POST /api/v1/workspaces, which runs bunkai_bootstrap_workspace: workspace and owner membership in one transaction.
  5. Alternatives to step 2-3: magic link or OAuth (GitHub, Google); both land on /auth/callback.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/auth/{check-email,signup,confirm,resend}, GET /auth/callback, POST /api/v1/workspaces

Entities touched: workspaces, workspace_members, access_tokens

Feature IDs: FEAT-001, FEAT-007 (legacy feature map)

Journey: machine sign-in and PAT lifecycle

A CLI, agent or pipeline gets a token without a browser, and its owner keeps credential hygiene: issue scoped tokens, list them, revoke them.

  1. Headless POST /api/v1/auth/signin returns a session and a PAT with DEFAULT_PAT_SCOPES, never workspace:admin.
  2. Extra tokens come from POST /api/v1/tokens in a cookie session. Issuance checks active membership in the target workspace and owner/admin role for workspace:admin; a global admin-scoped token is always refused.
  3. The raw secret is returned once; GET /api/v1/tokens lists tokens without secrets.
  4. A Bearer caller hitting /tokens gets 403: the posture is cookie-only.
  5. DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id} sets revoked_at; the next Bearer call with it fails immediately. The row stays for audit.
  6. Workspace switching (POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace) is also cookie-only: a PAT's workspace is fixed when it is minted (BK-316 regression check: a Bearer call there must be 403).

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/auth/signin, GET/POST /api/v1/tokens, DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}, POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace

Entities touched: access_tokens, workspace_members

Feature IDs: FEAT-002, FEAT-003, FEAT-005, FEAT-009 (legacy feature map)

Journey: workspace invite and acceptance

An owner or admin brings a teammate into the workspace with a chosen role.

  1. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites (owner/admin) generates a one-time token, stores only its SHA-256, and returns the raw token and accept_url.
  2. No email is sent: the admin shares the link by other means.
  3. The invitee signs in and calls POST /api/v1/invites/accept. The caller's auth email must equal the invite email.
  4. Membership and the acceptance stamp are written in one transaction. A revoked, already accepted or expired invite answers 409.
  5. Pending invites are listed and revoked under .../invites and .../invites/{inviteId}.

Endpoints involved: GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites, .../invites/{inviteId}, POST /api/v1/invites/accept

Entities touched: workspace_invites, workspace_members

Feature IDs: FEAT-010, FEAT-011 (legacy feature map)

Journey: ATC authoring, edit and bulk edit

Authors (people in the browser or agents with a PAT) build and maintain the Acceptance Test Cases that anchor every Test to a User Story.

  1. POST /api/v1/atcs (with an Idempotency-Key) runs bunkai_create_atc: the ATC, its steps, assertions and acceptance-criteria links in one transaction. Browser and machine use the same endpoint.
  2. PATCH /api/v1/atcs/{id} requires X-If-Match with the current version and answers 409 when stale. The browser edit path calls the same bunkai_update_atc RPC without a version (last write wins).
  3. POST /api/v1/atcs/bulk-edit changes one field (tags, module, layer or priority) on up to 200 ATCs of one project. Each ATC is processed on its own: partial success is normal and the report lists every outcome. Execution status is set by Runs and cannot be bulk-edited.
  4. Every ATC must stay anchored to at least one User Story and one acceptance criterion.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/atcs, PATCH /api/v1/atcs/{id}, POST /api/v1/atcs/bulk-edit, POST /api/v1/atcs/{id}/restore

Entities touched: atcs, atc_steps, atc_assertions, atc_acceptance_criteria

Feature IDs: FEAT-016, FEAT-017, FEAT-018 (legacy feature map); bulk edit has no legacy feature ID

Journey: run execution, evidence and bug filing

The heart of the product: a Test is executed and every step gets a result, with evidence, so failures become Bugs with full context.

  1. POST /api/v1/runs (cookie, or PAT with run:execute; Idempotency-Key required) snapshots the Test's ATC chain into run_atcs/run_steps. A cookie session runs as human; a PAT may declare agent or ci. A 24h same-token window returns the existing run instead of a duplicate.
  2. POST .../steps/{stepId}/mark records each step, in any order.
  3. Evidence is three calls: init the attachment, PUT the bytes to the signed Storage URL, then commit. The commit reads what actually arrived (size and real image type). PNG, JPEG or WebP only, 10 MiB per file, 50 MiB per step, 250 MiB per run. Uncommitted uploads are swept by the nightly cleanup job.
  4. POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/finish closes the run as passed or failed and marks untouched steps skipped. .../abort requires a reason.
  5. POST /api/v1/bugs with only run_step_id files a bug from a failed step; project, module, run and ATC are derived on the server.
  6. Agents can skip steps 1-4 with POST /api/v1/runs/submissions (Bearer only, run:execute): the run is created already finished, with step results keyed by chain position.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/runs, .../steps/{stepId}/mark, .../steps/{stepId}/attachments (+ /commit), .../finish, .../abort, POST /api/v1/runs/submissions, POST /api/v1/bugs

Entities touched: runs, run_atcs, run_steps, run attachments, bugs

Feature IDs: FEAT-029 to FEAT-034, FEAT-046 (legacy feature map); submissions and attachments have no legacy feature ID

Journey: Jira connection and story import

A team brings its backlog from its own Jira site into Bunkai, so ATCs can anchor to real User Stories (BK-1170 made the connection per workspace).

  1. PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/jira-connection (owner/admin: workspace:admin plus a live role check) saves site URL and email; the API token is write-only and stored in Supabase Vault. Saving does not call Jira.
  2. POST .../jira-connection/check tests the stored connection or unsaved values. Only https://<name>.atlassian.net is contacted. A failed test is a 200 with ok: false; one check at a time per person (429).
  3. POST /api/v1/imports (member, atc:write) returns 202 with a job id and runs the import after the response (Vercel after()), paging Jira and upserting stories and acceptance criteria.
  4. At most one active import per project: a second one answers 409. A workspace with no Jira connection also answers 409, with details.reason: jira_not_connected.
  5. GET/DELETE .../jira-connection reads (never the token) and disconnects.

Endpoints involved: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/jira-connection, POST .../jira-connection/check, POST /api/v1/imports, GET /api/v1/imports/{id}

Entities touched: workspace Jira connection (Vault secret), import jobs, user_stories, acceptance_criteria

Feature IDs: no legacy feature ID (the legacy feature map names it only as the Import feature)

Journey: plan upgrade through Stripe Checkout

The revenue path: a workspace owner upgrades the plan and pays with Stripe.

  1. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout is owner-only and requires an Idempotency-Key. The checkout-session row is written before Stripe is called; at most one open session per workspace (a second request reuses its URL or answers 409).
  2. The API creates the Stripe Checkout Session and returns its URL; the owner pays on Stripe.
  3. Stripe calls POST /api/v1/billing/webhook, authenticated only by its signature over the raw body.
  4. checkout.session.completed / async_payment_succeeded apply the plan only when Stripe's payment_status is paid; async_payment_failed and expired release the open-session lock. invoice.payment_failed / invoice.paid drive the failed-renewal grace window (BK-231).
  5. An event for a session not yet committed answers 5xx so Stripe redelivers it; other unknown events are acknowledged with 200.
  6. Maintenance routes: .../billing, details, invoices (+ PDF), payment-method, retry, checkout/cancel.

Endpoints involved: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout, POST /api/v1/billing/webhook (not in the OpenAPI spec), .../billing/*

Entities touched: billing_checkout_sessions, workspaces.plan, invoice events

Feature IDs: no legacy feature ID (billing post-dates the legacy feature map)

Architecture behind the API

The overview figure at the top shows the whole shape: three caller families, one gateway, Supabase behind it, three third parties. One Next.js 15 app on Vercel serves both the pages and the /api/v1 route handlers; there is no separate API gateway or service tier.

ComponentRolePersistence / integrations touchedWhy it matters for QA
withApiHandler()Posture gate, capability check, request id, error envelopeall routesA route answering outside the envelope, or reachable with the wrong posture, is a gateway bypass.
Principal resolution (principal.ts, middleware/bearer.ts)Bearer first, then cookie; mints a short-lived user JWT so PAT queries run under RLSaccess_tokensTest every route with both schemes where both are allowed; cookie-only routes must refuse a PAT.
Postgres + RLSWorkspace isolation for every query52 tables, 125 migrationsCross-workspace reads must come back empty or 404, never another tenant's rows.
SECURITY DEFINER RPCsAtomic multi-table writes (create ATC, create run, bootstrap workspace, billing events)129 distinct bunkai_* functions defined across migrationsNo partial saves: verify the rollback on a failing step, not only the happy path.
Idempotency keysReplay-safe creates13 mutating operations declare it (runs, ATCs, tests, bugs, projects, workspaces, billing, attachments)A missing header is a 400 idempotency_key_required, a replay returns the original resource.
Supabase VaultPer-workspace Jira API tokenread only by a service-role RPCThe token must never come back in any response.
Supabase StorageRun evidence imagesprivate bucket, service-role access after an RPC/RLS checkSigned upload URLs live 2 hours; uncommitted objects are swept nightly.
Vercel Cronsend-digest daily 08:00 UTC, storage-cleanup daily 03:00 UTCResend, StorageBoth are public routes guarded by CRON_SECRET: a call without it must be 401.
Background work (after())Jira import paging after the 202Jira, PostgresImport results arrive later: poll the job, do not assert right after the 202.

Discovery gaps

  • 409 jira_not_connected undocumented: POST /api/v1/imports answers it (route code), but the OpenAPI spec documents its 409 only as an import already running. Product contract gap for the dev team.
  • Stripe webhook not in the spec: POST /api/v1/billing/webhook exists in code and is not in /api/openapi.
  • Magic link cross-device not verified live: the callback supports token_hash, but whether the Supabase email template links with it is configured in the Supabase dashboard, not in the repo.
  • Pre-fix admin PATs (carried GAP-14): workspace:admin tokens minted on staging before the BK-134/135 fix were never confirmed revoked. Not re-queried in this pass.
  • Invite email: still not sent (route comment: MVP returns the link). Resend is wired only for the digest and the workspace deletion notice.
  • Journey cap: capped at 7. Left out despite being shipped: traceability and coverage reports, test plans, workspace chat, saved views, workspace deletion/restore/data export, notifications. Each deserves its own journey if the map is extended.
  • Placeholder companion maps: data, e2e, domain and infra maps are not generated, so entity and feature pointers above lean on legacy files that predate August 2026.
  • Storage bucket provenance: lib/storage/run-evidence-storage.ts notes its migration was pending apply when written; the bucket was not checked live in this pass.
  • Counts: route-posture counts are files containing each posture (some files are tests or OpenAPI fragments), not exact route counts.
